sources_considered.why: Primary paper documents the neural architecture, planning evaluation, limitations and a method for visualizing predicted representations.
Confirms authorship, LeCun’s involvement and the June 11, 2025 release date.
Primary announcement clarifies the demonstrated planning task and its image-goal interface.
Relevant contextual evidence that another team combined a JEPA-inspired text model with formal logic; it is not LeCun’s world-model implementation.
Discrete-JEPA modifies the framework for symbolic tasks. Its results cannot directly settle the claim about LeCun’s implementation.

evidence_items.locator: Section 2.1, Architecture; section 8, Future work; Appendix B.3, Visualizing World Model Predictions
evidence_items.explanation: The paper establishes the neural architecture, but its planning evaluations do not directly test formal inference over explicit structured knowledge. Appendix B.3 decodes predicted representations into visible frames, qualifying blanket uninterpretability without establishing a faithful explanation of internal reasoning.
Meta demonstrates planning toward image goals, with visual subgoals for longer tasks. This establishes a useful planning capability, but does not refute the contextual claim about formal reasoning.

Text-JEPA translates language into first-order logic and uses a Z3 solver for inference. This cautions against generalizing Marcus’s criticism to every JEPA-inspired system, but the added symbolic machinery and different implementation prevent direct contradiction.

unresolved_gaps: No located evaluation directly establishes poor suitability or demonstrated suitability of the targeted implementations for formal reasoning over structured world knowledge.
The sources do not supply a validated interpretability assessment matching Marcus’s broad wording.
Visualizing predictions does not establish faithful explanations of the internal operations that produced them.
Other teams’ symbolic extensions cannot settle the properties of LeCun’s existing implementation.
